title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
authors: Haozhe Liu, Tian Ye (equal contribution), Sensen Gao, Qihang Cao, Yitong Li (core contributors), Mingchen Zhuge, Duomin Wang, Ruihua Zhang, Ping Luo, Jiawang Bian, Lei Zhu, Ligeng Zhu, Enze Xie, Song Han
date: 17 September 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version on 3 October 2026)

code.title: NVlabs/SoL-Pi
code.note: The four mechanisms as an opt-in extension for Pi 0.85.1 (TypeScript, MIT licence, about 3,300 stars on 3 October 2026), with tests. Not released: the auto-research pipeline, the 535 search environments, the trajectories and the per-task EdgeBench results

run_label: replay a session through both harnesses
takeaway: Apply recursive self-improvement at the harness layer rather than to the model: auto-research loops across varied environments discover four reusable efficiency techniques (action execution, context compaction, observation handling, delegated reading) that cut recorded token traffic 44.7 to 49.0% at parity on EdgeBench, saving $8.75 to $13.50 per hour against native Codex and Claude Code.
verdict: Believe the mechanisms: they are released, small and inspectable, each one cut recorded tokens under both models, and the main cost saving reproduces from the paper's own token counts at list prices. Treat the numbers as single runs: no repeats or error bars, a score 2.5 to 2.8 points below Pi called "comparable", a "Performance" point picked on the test benchmark, a held-out score that includes the 11 tasks used for acceptance, hourly dollars that assume two-hour tasks, and 15 Terminal-Bench 4 tasks solved against Pi's 18.

headline.k: recorded token traffic against Pi on EdgeBench, GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5
headline.d: about 96% of it is cache reads, the cheapest kind of token

headline.k: API cost against Pi, for a score of 42.0 against 44.8 and 42.2 against 44.8
saved against native Codex and Claude Code ($4.36 to $5.71 against Pi)
headline.d: cost difference over 51 tasks × 2 hours: our derivation, not stated

resources.n: the method with more detail than the paper: all 152 proposal titles by family, the three orchestration designs that came before the disposable skill loop, ObservationPack's selection sweep and 11-task paired run, the humans' role, and the breadth-against-depth observation.

resources.by: ByteDance Seed (README, leaderboard and tech report arXiv 2607.05155)
resources.n: the held-out benchmark: 134 day-scale tasks, 51 public, scored as the best of many submissions within a time budget, with a stop hook so agents cannot quit early; its leaderboard is where the paper's GPT-5.5 @2h reference (31.2) comes from.

resources.t: Meta-Harness: end-to-end optimization of model harnesses
resources.n: the closest prior work: search over executable harness programs with a Pareto front of task score against context cost, tested on held-out datasets and models.

resources.t: Rethinking the evaluation of harness evolution for agents
resources.n: the study that motivates SoL-Pi's isolation rules: evolved harnesses overfit the tasks used in search and give marginal gains on unseen ones.

why recorded traffic and cost come apart: cache reads bill at a tenth of the input price and cache writes at 1.25 times it, so a rewritten prefix costs 12.5 times as much as a re-read one (the ratio Online Context Compact's gate uses).
the minimal, extensible harness SoL-Pi extends through public extension APIs; its native compaction is what Online Context Compact triggers.
the propose, implement, run, inspect, keep-or-discard loop each SoL-Pi lineage follows.

resources.t: Toward recursive self-improvement: how GLM built its own inference infrastructure
resources.n: the same week's production counterpart: GLM-5.3 as an Infra Agent tuned its own serving stack (3.22x throughput in 13 days) and the post's lesson is that the feedback environment, not the model, is the bottleneck. The post needs JavaScript; explainx.ai's summary is linked under Connections.
a hand-written view of the same problem the search automates: what a harness should do for an agent that runs for hours.

kb.t: Agora: Git as Shared Memory for Collective AutoResearch
kb.n: first of the week's three auto-research papers: many agents sharing one research record as Git commits.

kb.t: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
kb.n: third of the week's three: improve the exploration policy by replaying recorded search trees instead of paying for new evaluations; another way to make a self-improvement loop cheaper.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: a harness that versions its own prompts, memories and skills across trajectories: self-improvement aimed at capability rather than cost.
a hand-designed state-machine runbook around a fixed agent; it also reports cost, including a cheap model matching the frontier score at about 1/38 of the cost.

kb.t: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
kb.n: scores model-built harnesses on capability and execution-token cost, the two axes SoL-Pi's gates use.
the opposite design choice: a trained model writes a fresh harness per task, where SoL-Pi searches for one fixed harness that transfers.

kb.t: Proactive Memory Agent: selective reminding for long-horizon agents
kb.n: pulls the same lever the other way: Online Context Compact removes what the agent carries forward, selective reminding restores what it dropped.

kb.t: Latent Context Language Models (end-to-end context compression)
kb.n: context compression inside the model (soft tokens) rather than in the harness (summaries and handles).

kb.t: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
kb.n: another recursive harness-improvement loop, with regularisation against the overfitting SoL-Pi guards against by isolating EdgeBench.

topics.n: the five harness-scaling strategies it lists all optimise capability; SoL-Pi is the efficiency counterpart, and it runs the harness-improvement loop end to end that the topic page said nobody had run (since 2026-08-31).
EdgeBench, Terminal-Bench 4 and the IMO 2026 Lean setup used here.
prompt caching and the per-token prices that decide whether fewer tokens means a smaller bill.
